quote: So it's a single family home. Is there anybody oh, do you already have solar?
stewart_read: The moment the customer reveals existing solar, this call should branch into the orphaned_flow script (ownership status, panel size, system working status). The rep continues with a hybrid of standard verify questions instead of running the defined orphaned-flow checklist.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the standard verify questions (utility, bill, roof, credit) as still relevant regardless of orphaned status, which is partially true, but the schema-specific orphaned questions were never asked.
coaching_implication: Train reps to recognize the 'already have solar' trigger explicitly and switch scripts, not blend them ad hoc.

quote: if you've got some good ones, replacing some. I've got 10 that are twenty year over twenty five years old.
stewart_read: The rep captured that Gary owns his panels outright ('They're all mine') but never asked the two remaining hard-gate orphaned_flow questions: panel size/wattage and whether the current system is working. This is an incomplete qualification, not just a missed cross-sell — a broken/non-working existing system is a hard DQ per schema, and panel size affects design scope.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have felt the aging-panel detail was sufficient context to proceed, judging replacement intent as self-evidently qualifying.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always close out the orphaned_flow question set (owned/leased, company, panel size, working status) before moving to standard verify items — a broken existing system is a DQ the rep never checked for here.

quote: Do you have a credit score over 6 70?
stewart_read: Rep correctly states the 670 threshold matching the schema (unlike SESSION18_fcbf33c1's 650 drift), and gets a quick yes. Clean, compliant execution of this qualifier.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed here — this is the correct number and phrasing; can be used as a positive reference clip for reps who drift on the threshold.

quote: Are you able to access the power bill, like, online?
stewart_read: Rep asks for bill access after already having the $200 average bill figure, but does not flip that number into any emotional or urgency framing — it's asked and then immediately overtaken by the discovery that the bill was already sent elsewhere.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the call ends in duplicate-lead discovery seconds later, the rep may not have had a natural window to flip the bill before the call collapsed.
coaching_implication: Even in a short call, once the $200 figure was captured at 01:24 the rep had an opening to acknowledge bill pain before moving to document collection; that beat was skipped.

stewart_read: Gary reveals mid-call that he already sent a copy of his bill to another Ion contact ('Ella'), indicating a prior touchpoint the rep did not know about. The rep reacts with mild surprise ('Oh, to who?') but does not probe further — no attempt to confirm which rep, what was discussed, or reconcile records before ending the call.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged that once duplication was confirmed, no further probing added value and ending the call quickly avoided wasting the customer's time.
coaching_implication: Even in a duplicate-lead scenario, a quick confirmation of appointment date/time back to the customer would close the loop professionally instead of ending on 'sorry to bother you.'

quote: and then did you get scheduled?
stewart_read: The call ends with no recap, no confirmed date/time restated to the customer, and no text-follow-up promise — just an apology and goodbye once duplication is discovered.
alternative_hypothesis: Since Gary already has an appointment through another channel, a full button-up may be redundant; the strategic move would still be to confirm and restate the existing appointment for the customer's reassurance, which didn't happen.
coaching_implication: Coach reps that discovering a duplicate/already-scheduled lead should still end with a courtesy confirmation of the existing appointment details, not just a quick apology and hangup.
